title: George W. Bush Presidential Library: NSC and White House Press Office Records re: September 4, 2002 CBS News Report (David Martin) on Rumsfeld's 9/11 Notes and the NSA-Intercepted 9/11 Call to Georgia

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, and the Presidential Records Act, 44 U.S.C. §§ 2201–2209 (including § 2204(c)(1)), I request copies of records held by the George W. Bush Presidential Library concerning the White House and National Security Council (NSC) handling of a September 4, 2002 CBS News report by national security correspondent David Martin. The report described notes taken by aides to Secretary of Defense Donald Rumsfeld on September 11, 2001. It also described a call intercepted by the National Security Agency at about 9:53 a.m. that day, from a bin Laden operative in Afghanistan to a telephone number in the Republic of Georgia.

For context: 

An article about David Martin's investigation into the intercepted telephone call is still hosted by CBS and can be found online at the link below, with the mention of the telephone call to Georgia mentioned in the third paragraph:
https://www.cbsnews.com/news/plans-for-iraq-attack-began-on-9-11/

A recording of this episode of the CBS Evening News that featured David Martin's report is currently hosted by YouTube at the link below. The mention of the call is in the first few minutes of the report:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xMScjLDVO8E


1. Scope:

All textual and electronic records (emails, attachments, memoranda, press guidance including "if-asked" guidance, talking points, Q&As, briefing and gaggle preparation materials, press inquiry and call logs, phone message slips, and drafts) dated September 3, 2002 through September 10, 2002, inclusive, that were sent to, sent from, copied to, or maintained by:

a. The NSC Press Office and NSC communications staff, including the NSC spokesperson and director-level press staff, and any assistants or detailees, specifically including Anna M. Perez and Sean McCormack 

b. The White House Office of the Press Secretary, including Ari Fleischer, Scott McClellan and Claire Buchan, and the Office of Communications, including Dan Bartlett;

c. NSC European and Eurasian Affairs staff, including Daniel Fried and Matthew Bryza, to the extent they contributed to guidance on Georgia or the Pankisi Gorge; and

d. Condoleezza Rice and Stephen Hadley, limited to communications concerning press response to the CBS report.

Records are responsive if they contain any of the following terms in the subject line, body or attachments: "CBS"; "David Martin"; "Pankisi"; "Duisi"; "Georgia" or "Tbilisi" or "Shevardnadze" or "Menagarishvili" or "Japaridze" or "Ambassador Japardize" (each in proximity to "intercept," "NSA," "Afghanistan" or "9/11"); "Rumsfeld" in proximity to "notes," "Cambone" or "Iraq"; "Saddam" or "S.H." in proximity to "UBL," "9/11" or "September 11"; "sweep it all up"; "go massive."

I also request records reflecting any inquiry to NSA, CIA or the Department of Defense about the accuracy or sourcing of the CBS report, to the extent held in the files described above.

2. Context:

The CBS report ran on September 4, 2002, as the administration was making its public case on Iraq. I seek the internal communications, press inquiries and guidance created in the days before and after the broadcast.

3. Format, Review and Exemptions

Please provide records electronically as searchable PDFs. Release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b). For anything withheld, please provide an itemized description identifying each record and the exemption claimed. A logical assumption is that any material prepared for release to, or in response to question from, a member of the news media would be, by definition, not classified. However, if any responsive material is classified, please treat this letter as a request for mandatory declassification review under E.O. 13526 § 3.5. If any records or portions are referred to NSA, CIA or DoD for consultation, please notify me of the referral and the receiving agency.

I am an amateur researcher, and I intend to disseminate the results publicly, including through MuckRock. I am not requesting for commercial use. I ask that fees be waived under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(iii), because release would contribute significantly to public understanding of how the September 11 attacks and Iraq were presented to the public.

Thank you for the work that the George W. Bush Presidential Library does and thank you for the commitment to transparency.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware
